clue.text: Urchin found torn mag in funfair roundabout

indicators.note: the word in tells us one scrambled group sits inside the other
a roundabout goes round and round, so the letters of funfair are turned about into a new order
something torn is ripped apart, so the letters of mag are rearranged

explanation.surface: A street kid is discovered among shredded magazines on a fairground carousel.
explanation.walkthrough: 'funfair roundabout' looks like a fairground ride, but 'roundabout' only signals a rearrangement of the word before it.
explanation.definitionFit: Both words describe a ragged, scruffy street child, so they are synonyms.

clue.text: Fellow coming in to recycle rubbish

indicators.note: coming in means one piece enters the middle of the other

parts.note: to recycle something is to use it again

explanation.surface: A man arrives at the dump to sort out the household waste.
explanation.walkthrough: 'coming in' puts F inside REUSE.
explanation.definitionFit: Waste material thrown away is called both rubbish and refuse, a direct synonym.

clue.text: Excessively bright nameless embellishment

indicators.note: nameless means without a name, and N is the usual abbreviation for name, so that letter goes

parts.note: a garnish is a decorative addition, especially on food

explanation.surface: An anonymous decoration is far too loud and colourful.
explanation.walkthrough: 'nameless' removes N (name) from GARNISH.
explanation.definitionFit: Gaudy colours that are overly vivid and showy are described with this adjective.

clue.text: Prosaic in reality

definitions.meaning: prosaic means plain, unimaginative and down-to-earth
the phrase used adverbially in 'as a ___', meaning actually or in truth

explanation.walkthrough: The second sense uses the phrase in 'as a matter of fact', meaning really.
explanation.definitionFit: An unemotional, practical person is described this way, and the same phrase means actually.

clue.text: Experienced hat-maker

definitions.meaning: past tense of feel, meaning underwent or sensed
a matted woollen fabric from which hats such as trilbies and fedoras are made

explanation.walkthrough: 'hat-maker' looks like a milliner, but here it is the material that makes hats.
explanation.definitionFit: Sensed or underwent is the past tense of feel; the matted cloth is used for hats.

clue.text: Balls bowled by popular footballer on board

parts.note: something popular is said to be in

indicators.note: being on board means being placed within a ship, so the ship's letters wrap round the player

parts.note: SS stands for steamship, the vessel one is aboard
a winger is a footballer who plays out on the flank

explanation.surface: A well-liked football player on a club's board makes some cricket deliveries.
explanation.walkthrough: 'on board' is the convention for going inside SS, a steamship. In cricket, a bowler delivers balls; inswingers curve in towards the batsman.
explanation.definitionFit: These are cricket deliveries that swerve in the air towards the batter.

clue.text: A cut-price ticket a long way off

indicators.note: a cut item loses its last part, so the final letter is removed

parts.note: a fare is the price of a travel ticket

explanation.surface: A discounted ticket for a distant destination.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cut-price' reads as one discount word, but 'cut' docks the last letter of the fare.
explanation.definitionFit: Distance at a remove, as in 'from a great distance', is the sense of this adverb.

clue.text: Bird's ring of fire

parts.note: on fire is flaming
O is ring-shaped

explanation.surface: A bird appears to own a circle of flames.
explanation.walkthrough: The 's is 'is': the bird is O of FLAMING, written FLAMING then O.
explanation.definitionFit: This pink wading bird of lagoons is an example of a bird.

clue.text: Varying tones are to resound

indicators.note: varying means changing, so the letters of these two words are reordered

explanation.surface: Different musical tones are made to ring out.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Varying' rearranges TONES and ARE.
explanation.definitionFit: To echo or ring loudly is a synonym, both verbs of sound carrying and reverberating.

clue.text: Way to travel on A1?

parts.note: the A1 is a major British road, but A1 also means top-quality, so the best way to travel

explanation.surface: A query about how to drive up the A1, Britain's long north-south trunk road.
explanation.walkthrough: A1 here means excellent, so the top-grade way to travel on trains or planes.
explanation.definitionFit: The premium tier of travel on trains and planes is excellent, just as A1 means excellent.

clue.text: Bachelor's second fish

parts.note: BA is a bachelor's degree (Bachelor of Arts), and the 's gives S

explanation.surface: An unmarried man's second fish of the day.
explanation.walkthrough: BA (Bachelor of Arts) plus the S of 's, then S for second.
explanation.definitionFit: The sea bass is a common edible species, an example of a fish.

clue.text: Go mad when it is not affecting the whole

parts.note: to go is to depart
mental is informal for mad

explanation.surface: Advice on going crazy when something only partly applies.
explanation.definitionFit: Something limited to one section or division of an organisation does not involve all of it.

clue.text: Resist being corrupted by one of the family

indicators.note: something corrupted is altered from its true form, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Fight off being led astray by a relative.
explanation.walkthrough: 'being corrupted' rearranges RESIST.
explanation.definitionFit: A female sibling is a member of one's family, an example of a relative.

clue.text: Emil broke new link at furnace

indicators.note: something broke is smashed apart, so the letters of the name are rearranged
new means remade in a fresh form, so the letters of link are rearranged

explanation.surface: Emil snapped a fresh chain link at the forge.
explanation.walkthrough: 'broke' turns EMIL into LIME; 'new' turns LINK into KILN.
explanation.definitionFit: A kiln for burning limestone into quicklime is a kind of furnace.

clue.text: So inspired about range of deviation

indicators.note: about can mean around or in a different arrangement, so these letters are mixed up

explanation.surface: Feeling so motivated about the spread of variation.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' rearranges SO INSPIRED.
explanation.definitionFit: In statistics, the spread of values around a mean is measured as this quantity.

clue.text: It is not still being fired at

definitions.text: It is not still being fired at

parts.words: It is not still being fired at
parts.note: something shot at which keeps going rather than standing still; still looks like 'yet' but means motionless

explanation.surface: Reads as if something has stopped being fired at.
explanation.walkthrough: 'still' reads as 'any longer' but means stationary.
explanation.definitionFit: A target in motion is one that is not stationary while being shot at.

clue.text: Deliberate swindle on partisan

parts.note: a con is a swindle
a sider is one who takes a side, a partisan

explanation.surface: A calculated fraud practised on a supporter.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Deliberate' looks like an adjective, but it is the verb meaning to think over.
explanation.definitionFit: To deliberate is to think carefully about something, a synonym of the verb.

clue.text: Hard time when one entered theatre

indicators.note: entered means went into, so one word goes inside the other

parts.note: the stage stands for the theatre as a profession

explanation.surface: A difficult period began when someone went into acting.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Hard time' looks like a spell of hardship, but it is an era named after a hard material.
explanation.definitionFit: The prehistoric era when tools were made of rock is a period named after a hard material.

clue.text: Feeling depressed without whisky, rum etc.

definitions.meaning: literally having run out of distilled liquors

explanation.walkthrough: Spirits means both mood and strong liquor.
explanation.definitionFit: Being low in mood is the idiom; lacking strong liquor is the literal sense.

clue.text: Keep cheerful feature at university

parts.note: the chin is a facial feature
up means in residence at university, as in 'up at Oxford'

explanation.surface: A student's facial trait helps them stay positive.
explanation.walkthrough: In British usage, being up means attending university.
explanation.definitionFit: The exhortation is an idiom urging someone to stay brave and cheerful.

clue.text: Spaniard embraces international elder

indicators.note: embraces means holds within, so one piece goes inside another

parts.note: señor is a Spanish man, the form of address

explanation.surface: A man from Spain hugs a veteran of the national team.
explanation.walkthrough: 'embraces' puts I inside SENOR.
explanation.definitionFit: An older person, or one higher in rank by age, is a synonym of elder.

clue.text: Cushy job at home in safe environment

indicators.note: an environment surrounds something, so the safe word wraps round the home word

parts.note: safe means secure
at home is in

explanation.surface: An easy post working from home in a protected setting.
explanation.definitionFit: A post with pay but little work is a soft, easy position.

clue.text: Compensate chieftain retaining expert in applied science

indicators.note: retaining means holding within, so the letters are found inside these words

explanation.surface: Pay off a clan leader who is keeping a scientist on the payroll.
explanation.walkthrough: 'retaining' signals the run spanning the end of Compensate and the start of chieftain.
explanation.definitionFit: Informally, a technical specialist, especially in computing, is called this.

clue.text: Just yours truly again

parts.note: yours truly is a jocular way of saying me
re- is a prefix meaning again

explanation.surface: Only me once more.
explanation.definitionFit: Only or simply, as in 'a mere child', is the adjective's sense.

clue.text: Drink prescribed by doctor early in the day

parts.note: a.m. denotes the morning

explanation.surface: A tipple recommended by the GP for the morning.
explanation.definitionFit: A small measure of whisky or spirits is a drink.

clue.text: Diane, the Parisian teetotaller, was not in favour of those who dabble

parts.note: Di is a short form of Diane
le is French for the
TT stands for teetotal, a teetotaller
anti means against, opposed to

explanation.surface: A non-drinking French woman named Diane disapproved of amateurs.
explanation.definitionFit: Plural of an Italian loanword for amateurs who take up an art superficially.

clue.text: Regretted impolite sound

indicators.note: sound here signals that the word is said aloud and a like-sounding word is entered

parts.note: impolite means rude

explanation.surface: Was sorry for a bad-mannered noise.
explanation.walkthrough: 'sound' looks like a noun after impolite, but it signals the like-sounding word.
explanation.definitionFit: Felt sorry about is the past tense of rue, a synonym.

clue.text: Cover runner, one who has not been invited

definitions.text: one who has not been invited

parts.note: to inter is to bury, covering with earth
a loper runs with long strides

explanation.surface: A substitute athlete turns out to be a gatecrasher.
explanation.definitionFit: An intruder who pushes into places or affairs where unwelcome is a synonym.
